<cite ref="Aramaic Targum to Ecclesiastes 10:8">Targ. Koh. X, 8</cite> <he>ג׳ דעלמא</he> the world’s fence (morality).—
ib. I, 1) it means ג׳ wall (not פלוגתא division). Ib. 36ᵃ מג׳ דערודי ולבר the land outside the fence which is erected to protect the fields from beasts.
<cite ref="Shabbat 110b:3">Sabb. 110ᵇ</cite> <he>בין תנורא לג׳</he> between the stove and the wall.
<cite ref="Taanit 21a:2">Taan. 21ᵃ</cite> <he>ג׳ רעיעא</he> (Ms. M.; <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Torah 897:10">Yalk. Deut. 897</cite> <he>אשיתא</he>) a ruinous wall.
<cite ref="Kohelet Rabbah 10:7">Koh. R. to X, 7</cite> <he>טריף רישיה אג׳</he> he knocked his head against the wall.
<cite ref="Bava Kamma 92b:14">B. Kam. 92ᵇ</cite> (prov.) <he>קרית חברך … רמי ג׳ רבה שדי ביה</he> (Ms. M. <he>דחי גידא רבא וכ׳</he>, Ms. R. a.

<cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Nach 364:2">Yalk. Ez. 364</cite> <he>דחי ג׳ רמי שדי עילויה</he>) when thou hast called thy neighbor (cautioning him), and he would not answer, push down a big wall and throw it at him (he deserves to suffer).—Pl. with suff. <he>גּוּדָּהָא</he>.
